updates.summary: Vitest 4 replaced vitest.workspace.ts / defineWorkspace with test.projects in the main config.
changes: Key Concepts — "Workspace config" example (`vitest.workspace.ts`, `defineWorkspace`) → `test.projects` in `vitest.config.ts` with `extends: true`; `vitest --project unit` unchanged.

updates.summary: setupFiles run before every test file, not once.
changes: TL;DR — "Setup files run once before test files" → they run before each test file.

updates.summary: Vitest 4 removed environmentMatchGlobs; per-directory environments now use test.projects.
changes: TL;DR — mention of `environmentMatchGlobs` → `test.projects`.
Key Concepts — `environmentMatchGlobs` example replaced by `projects` entries with `environment` + `include`.
Coding Challenge — challenge text and solution use `projects` (node and jsdom) instead of `environmentMatchGlobs`; comment in the test file updated.

updates.summary: coverage.all was removed in Vitest 4; coverage.include now decides which untested files appear.
changes: Key Concepts — `all: true` removed from the coverage config, with a note that `coverage.include` controls whether untested files show up as 0%.

updates.summary: In Vitest 4 a mock called with `new` needs a function/class implementation, not an arrow function.
changes: Key Concepts — `PrismaClient: vi.fn().mockImplementation(() => ({...}))` → `mockImplementation(function () { return {...} })` with a note on the "is not a constructor" error.

updates.summary: In Vitest 4, vi.restoreAllMocks() only restores vi.spyOn spies and no longer clears or resets mock state.
changes: Key Concepts — `restoreAllMocks` section: removed "Clears call tracking / Resets implementations"; spy.mock.calls is no longer cleared by it.
Key Concepts — global-methods comment `= mockRestore() on every spy` replaced with the Vitest 4 behaviour.
Interview Q&A — "restoreAllMocks does everything reset does, plus restore" → it only restores spyOn originals (Vitest 4).
Coding Challenge / recap — RESET VS CLEAR VS RESTORE summary line updated.

updates.summary: Vitest 4 browser mode: playwright() provider factory, instances, vitest/browser imports, and projects instead of a workspace file.
changes: Key Concepts — install is `@vitest/browser-playwright`; config uses `provider: playwright()` and `instances: [{ browser: "chromium" }]` instead of `provider: "playwright"` + `name`.
Key Concepts — "Workspace config" (`vitest.workspace.ts`) → `test.projects` in `vitest.config.ts`; `import { userEvent } from "@vitest/browser/context"` → `"vitest/browser"`.
Why It Matters / Common Pitfalls — "workspace" wording and the `userEvent` import updated.
Coding Challenge — challenge and solution rewritten for `projects`, `playwright()`, and `vitest/browser`.

updates.summary: Vitest's `page` is its own browser-side locator API, not the Playwright Page; page.locator() and Playwright-style assertions do not exist.
changes: TL;DR — removed the claim of "full Playwright `page` access via `vi.importActual`"; `page` comes from `vitest/browser` and is not the raw Playwright Page.
Key Concepts — Playwright config updated for Vitest 4 (`playwright({ launchOptions, contextOptions })`, `headless` on `browser`, `instances`); `providerOptions.launch/context` removed.
Key Concepts — `page.locator("#x")` / `expect(locator)` examples → `page.getByRole` / `getByTestId` with `await expect.element(...)`; `page.screenshot()` returns a file path, not a Buffer.
Key Concepts — cross-browser example uses `browser.instances` instead of a workspace with `name`.
Common Pitfalls / Coding Challenge — launch args via `launchOptions`; challenge solution uses `getByTestId`, `expect.element`, and `vitest/browser` imports.

updates.summary: Browser-mode imports and locator usage updated for Vitest 4.
changes: Key Concepts — "(via workspace config)" → a browser project via `test.projects`.
Coding Challenge — `@vitest/browser/context` → `vitest/browser`; `page.locator("#name")` → `page.getByPlaceholder(...)` with `expect.element`.

updates.summary: End-of-day browser-mode recap updated for Vitest 4.
changes: Coding Challenge / recap — BROWSER MODE block: `provider: "playwright"` → `playwright()` + `instances`, `@vitest/browser playwright` → `@vitest/browser-playwright`, `@vitest/browser/context` → `vitest/browser`, `page.locator` / `expect(locator)` → `getByRole`/`expect.element`.

updates.summary: Vitest 4 removed poolOptions (maxThreads/singleFork) in favour of top-level maxWorkers, and the default pool is forks, not threads.
changes: TL;DR — default pool and sizing: `threads` default / `singleThread` → `forks` default, top-level `maxWorkers`, `maxWorkers: 1` or `fileParallelism: false` for serial runs.
Key Concepts — `poolOptions.threads/forks` config replaced by top-level `maxWorkers`; serial example no longer uses `singleThread`; "choosing the right pool" now lists forks as the default.
Why It Matters / Interview Q&A — `maxThreads` → `maxWorkers`; "use threads (the default)" corrected (forks is the default).
Coding Challenge — `vitest.workspace.ts` + `poolOptions` solution → `test.projects` with `maxWorkers` / `fileParallelism: false`.

updates.summary: setupFiles run before every test file; the lesson contradicted itself by calling it once per worker.
changes: TL;DR / Key Concepts — "setupFiles once-per-worker" → runs before each test file (cheap setup only).
Why It Matters / Interview Q&A — cost reasoning changed from "once per worker thread (8 times on 8 cores)" to "once per test file".
Common Pitfalls — heading and comment "runs N times (once per worker)" → once per test file.

updates.summary: Pool recap and challenge config updated to Vitest 4 top-level pool options.
changes: Coding Challenge — config uses `pool: "forks"`, `maxWorkers`, `isolate` instead of `pool: "threads"` + `poolOptions.threads`; challenge text says "projects" for separate pools.
Coding Challenge / recap — WORKER POOLS block: default pool, `maxWorkers`, and serial execution (`maxWorkers: 1` / `fileParallelism: false`) updated; setupFiles line says "before every test file".

updates.summary: next/image `priority` is deprecated in Next.js 16 in favour of `preload`.
changes: Coding Challenge — challenge text and `HeroBanner` solution: `priority` → `preload`, comment no longer claims it sets fetchpriority.

updates.summary: next/image `priority` is deprecated in Next.js 16 in favour of `preload` (which only adds the preload link).
changes: Key Concepts — `priority` examples and decision table → `preload` (with `loading="eager"` / `fetchPriority="high"` as the usual alternatives).
Why It Matters — claim that `priority` sets fetchpriority and disables lazy loading replaced with what `preload` actually does.
Coding Challenge / recap — hero image solution and KEY RULES use `preload`.

updates.summary: `npm ci --frozen-lockfile` is not an npm flag.

updates.summary: `npm ci --frozen-lockfile` is not an npm flag.
